claims.text: The as-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The as-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The as-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 contains a continuous brittle B2 phase.
The continuous B2 phase limits strain hardening and deformation uniformity in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The continuous B2 phase causes rapid failure of HfZrTiTa0.53 under dynamic loading.
A short anneal at approximately 600°C can invert the phase topology from a continuous B2 phase to discrete nanoscale B2 precipitates in a continuous disordered BCC matrix.
The annealed HfZrTiTa0.53 microstructure will consist of discrete nanoscale B2 precipitates within a continuous BCC matrix.
Disrupting the continuous B2 network will enable more homogeneous dislocation activity.
More homogeneous dislocation activity will enhance strain hardening.
Dispersed B2 precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion and thereby strengthen the alloy.
Dispersed B2 precipitates will redistribute stress and delay shear localization.
Annealed HfZrTiTa0.53 will have a higher dynamic strain-hardening rate than the as-cast baseline.
Annealed HfZrTiTa0.53 will sustain more uniform plastic deformation than the as-cast baseline.
Annealed HfZrTiTa0.53 will have higher dynamic compressive strength than the as-cast baseline.
Annealed HfZrTiTa0.53 will absorb more impact energy than the as-cast baseline.
Annealed HfZrTiTa0.53 will delay adiabatic shear localization and rapid failure at strain rates of 10^3–10^4 s^-1.
The prediction applies from room temperature to moderately elevated temperatures under high-strain-rate adiabatic loading.
Excessive grain growth or undesirable secondary-phase formation would remove or reduce the expected benefit.
The optimal annealing temperature, annealing duration, and magnitude of dynamic-property improvement are unknown.

contradictions.description: The prediction concerns increased impact-energy absorption, while the measurement list parenthetically equates energy absorption with 'impact-induced energy release.' Absorbed and released energy are distinct quantities, so the targeted energetic outcome is not consistently defined.
